item.title: Decode: 0F B6 04 11
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64. Decode this instruction: 0F B6 04 11. What is the assembly? Why is there no REX prefix, and what size is the memory read versus the register written?
Answer: movzx eax, byte ptr [rcx+rdx] - 0F is the two-byte opcode escape; 0F B6 = MOVZX r32, r/m8. ModRM 04 = 00 000 100: mod=00 (no disp), reg=000 (eax, destination), rm=100 (SIB follows). - SIB 11 = 00 010 001: scale=1, index=rdx, base=rcx. Addresses are 64-bit by default, so no REX is needed. - Only 1 byte is read from memory; it is zero-extended into eax, and the 32-bit write also clears the upper half of rax.
